about: Rockhound Scout known sites: well-known collecting spots added to a Custom search when the search area covers them. 'fee': true = pay-to-dig (only shown when the customer turns on 'Include pay-to-dig sites'). 'approx': true = location is approximate (within a mile or two) and is used only to decide which searches include the site; the Google Maps button searches by 'mapQuery'. Reviewed by JT before use.

sites.name: Baby Head Ridge Llanite Dike Roadcut — TX-16 Northbound
sites.rock: Llanite dike (porphyritic rhyolite, ~1.106 billion years old) cutting Valley Spring Gneiss
sites.where: Roadcut at the crest of a low ridge about 9 miles north of Llano on TX-16 — the llanite dike cuts across the highway through the surrounding Valley Spring Gneiss.
finds: Llanite (blue quartz phenocrysts — world type locality)
sites.directions: From the Llano courthouse square, take TX-16 north about 9 miles. Baby Head Cemetery will be on your right (east side). Continue a short distance further north to a small gravel pullout at the roadcut — park there, not on the highway shoulder.
sites.truck: Watch for a low, dark ridge notching across the highway — the llanite is distinctly darker and more blocky than the pale pinkish-tan gneiss around it. Fractured boulders and rock fragments are visible at the roadcut on both sides of the pavement.
sites.why: This roadcut is the world type locality for llanite — its striking blue quartz phenocrysts get their color from microscopic ilmenite inclusions, and this rock is found nowhere else on Earth.
sites.access: Roadside right-of-way only. Do not climb fences; the land on both sides is private.

sites.name: Crystal Vista — Free Quartz Crystal Site (Ouachita National Forest)
sites.rock: Quartz veins in Ouachita Mountain sandstone and shale
sites.where: A 4-acre former commercial crystal mine on top of Gardner Mountain, now a National Forest site where quartz crystals can be collected from the ground surface.
sites.directions: From Mount Ida, head south on AR-27 for 3.8 miles, then turn left (east) onto County Road 2237 (Owley Road). Continue 4.1 miles to the Crystal Vista trailhead.
sites.truck: Look for the trailhead parking at the end of the directions; the old mine spoil is a short walk up Gardner Mountain. No water at the site.
sites.why: One of the few free public places in the Ouachitas to pick up quartz crystals. Surface collecting only — check current Forest Service rules before you dig.
sites.access: Ouachita National Forest. Call the Caddo-Womble Ranger District at (870) 867-2101 for current collecting rules.
sites.mapQuery: Crystal Vista Trailhead, Mount Ida, AR

sites.name: Crater of Diamonds State Park — Dig for Real Diamonds
sites.rock: Eroded surface of a volcanic lamproite pipe
sites.where: The only public diamond-bearing site in the world where visitors keep what they find.
sites.directions: The park is about 2 miles southeast of Murfreesboro, Arkansas. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions.
sites.truck: Follow the park signs to the visitor center; you pay and get digging rules there.
sites.why: Visitors pay a small admission fee to search the 37-acre plowed field and keep any gemstone they find, regardless of value.
sites.access: Arkansas state park — admission fee to dig. Collecting is allowed only in the search field.
sites.mapQuery: Crater of Diamonds State Park, Murfreesboro, AR

sites.name: Wegner Crystal Mines — Pay-to-Dig Quartz
sites.rock: Quartz veins in Ouachita Mountain rock
sites.where: A family-run commercial quartz crystal mine south of Mount Ida, the 'Quartz Crystal Capital of the World.'
sites.directions: Wegner Crystal Mines is just south of Mount Ida off AR-27. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions, and call ahead for hours and fees.
sites.truck: Watch for the Wegner Crystal Mines signs off AR-27.
sites.why: A commercial mine with dig-your-own options for quartz crystals.
sites.access: Private commercial mine — fee to dig. Call ahead for hours.
sites.mapQuery: Wegner Crystal Mines, Mount Ida, AR

sites.name: Herkimer Diamond Mines — Pay-to-Dig
sites.where: The best-known Herkimer diamond dig, on NY-28 north of Herkimer near Middleville.
sites.directions: From Herkimer, take NY-28 north about 7 miles toward Middleville. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions.
sites.truck: Watch for the Herkimer Diamond Mines signs and gift shop on NY-28.
sites.why: Herkimer diamonds weather out of cavities in the Little Falls Dolostone; this commercial mine lets visitors split rock and keep what they find.
sites.access: Private commercial mine — fee to dig. Seasonal; check hours before you go.
sites.mapQuery: Herkimer Diamond Mines, 4601 State Route 28, Herkimer, NY

sites.name: Ace of Diamonds Mine — Pay-to-Dig
sites.where: A commercial Herkimer diamond mine on NY-28 just south of Middleville.
sites.directions: From Herkimer, take NY-28 north past the Herkimer Diamond KOA campground; the mine entrance is a little further on the left. It's easy to miss — use the Google Maps button.
sites.truck: Watch for mining equipment on a hill on the left side of NY-28.
sites.why: Another long-running commercial dig in the same Herkimer-diamond-bearing dolostone.
sites.access: Private commercial mine — fee to dig. Seasonal; check hours before you go.
sites.mapQuery: Ace of Diamonds Mine, Middleville, NY

sites.name: Crystal Grove Diamond Mine — Pay-to-Dig
sites.where: A Herkimer diamond dig and campground north of St. Johnsville.
sites.directions: In St. Johnsville, turn onto County Route 114 North and follow the Crystal Grove signs to the campground on the right. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions.
sites.truck: Watch for Crystal Grove signs; there is a small store and parking lot.
sites.why: A commercial dig in the Herkimer-diamond-bearing Little Falls Dolostone.
sites.access: Private commercial mine — fee to dig. Seasonal; check hours before you go.
sites.mapQuery: Crystal Grove Diamond Mine, St. Johnsville, NY

sites.name: Topaz Mountain Rockhound Area (BLM) — Free
sites.where: A BLM rockhound recreation area in the Thomas Range about 55 miles northwest of Delta.
sites.directions: From Delta, take US-6 west, then follow the paved county road north to the Thomas Range. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions; there are no services out there.
sites.truck: Look for the BLM rockhound area signs below Topaz Mountain; collect in the gravels and rhyolite cavities.
sites.why: A designated BLM rockhound area known for sherry-colored topaz crystals. No facilities; dispersed camping is allowed.
sites.access: BLM public land — free. Personal collecting under BLM rules. Fillmore Field Office: 435-743-3100.

sites.name: U-Dig Fossils — Pay-to-Dig Trilobites
sites.where: A private trilobite quarry near Antelope Springs in the House Range, about 52 miles west of Delta.
sites.directions: From Delta, drive 32 miles west on US-6/50 and turn north at the U-Dig Fossils sign between mile markers 56 and 57. Follow the 20-mile gravel road and the U-Dig signs.
sites.truck: Watch for the U-Dig Fossils sign between mile markers 56 and 57 on US-6/50.
sites.why: One of the best-known places in the country to split shale and keep your own trilobites.
sites.access: Private quarry — fee to dig. Open about mid-April to mid-October, weather permitting.

sites.name: Caspersen Beach — Free Shark Tooth Hunting
sites.rock: Fossil-rich Gulf beach sands (Peace River Formation fossils)
sites.where: A Sarasota County beach park at the south end of Venice, the 'Shark Tooth Capital of the World.'
sites.directions: Caspersen Beach Park is at 4100 Harbor Drive South in Venice, at the south end of Harbor Drive. Use the Google Maps button for turn-by-turn directions.
sites.truck: Park in the beach lot; sift the shell line at the water's edge.
sites.why: Fossil shark teeth wash up here every day; a sifting scoop at the waterline is the classic way to find them.
sites.access: Sarasota County park. Check park rules; collecting loose shark teeth on the beach is a long-standing tradition here.
sites.mapQuery: Caspersen Beach Park, 4100 Harbor Dr S, Venice, FL
